Worrell, E., Phylipsen, D., Einstein, D. and Martin, N. (2000). Energy Use and Energy Intensity of the U.S. Chemical Industry. Report LBNL-44314, Ernest Orlando Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, Berkeley, CA, April 2000. No DOI printed.

Locators are printed page numbers (equal to PDF page numbers). Data are for the U.S. 1994-1996 (survey and MECS data), not Canada. Main file: steam-cracker energy per tonne ethylene (modern-plant text values, Tables 12, 14, 15, U.S. average; feedstock excluded; mixed carriers so target blank) and investment per feedstock (1993 USD, Gielen et al. 1996); ammonia SEC from the Fertilizer Institute survey and the Table 16 balance plus modern reforming and partial-oxidation values and a greenfield cost; nitric-acid N2O factor; chlorine SEC by cell type (Table 5, steam + electricity per t chlorine) and the U.S. average (Table 17); Table 6 SECs including feedstock (ethylene+co-products, methanol, ammonia, urea, N2, O2); Table 3 plastics energy (two estimates). Not loaded to main: sector totals and production, primary-energy figures (Table 13 is labelled primary), sub-process breakdowns, Table 7 yields, production costs (other-values). Traps: (1) Table 16 gas column sums to 35.0 GJ/t but the Summary gives feedstock 20.4 + fuel 15.2 = 35.6. (2) Table 5 electricity per cell (2720-3420 kWh/t) is lower than the Table 17 U.S. average (4380 kWh/t); Table 17 includes rectifier, cooling, compression and a 10% age penalty. (3) Footnote 15 says primary energy assumes 40% power efficiency, Table 5 and the abstract use 33%; Chapter 6 gives 36.6 GJ/t LHV for ammonia where the abstract gives 37.1. (4) Table 6 plastics SECs equal Table 3 Estimate 1 and were loaded once (as Table 3); Estimate 2 (LDPE 1.6, PP 1.2) is far lower, probably electricity only or best practice. (5) Heating-value basis is stated for only some rows; Table 3 and Tables 12-14 are not stated. (6) Table 14 is attributed to Di Cintio et al. 1993 in the text and 1992 in the caption.
